title: Cleary Gottlieb to roll out Legora across the firm
author: Legal IT Insider

dom.t: Legora partnerships: Adoption needs selected workflows and training

st.t: Legora partnerships: Adoption needs selected workflows and training
st.an: The source supports the cluster’s platform-led adoption narrative through Cleary’s planned firmwide Legora rollout, while reinforcing that deployment should focus on identified, high-value workflows and coexist with proprietary AI development. Its efficiency and client-service claims are expectations rather than measured outcomes, consistent with the cluster’s distinction between rollout and demonstrated benefits.
qs: The strategic partnership will see Cleary roll out Legora’s suite of AI-driven services, including new product features, across the firm.

“This is not about simply rolling out AI across the firm, but about engaging with identified, high-value use cases that enhance our ability to serve clients across practices, teams, and regions.”  To date, Legora has raised over $35m in funding from investors, including Benchmark, Redpoint, SV Angel, Y Combinator, and others.

kp.k: Cleary moves from pilot to firmwide AI rollout
kp.d: The article reports that Cleary Gottlieb announced its partnership with Legora on 1 May 2025, following a pilot described as successful in 2024. The planned rollout covers Legora’s suite of AI-driven services and new product features across the firm; the article supplies no pilot performance measures.
qs: announced today (1 May) that it has signed up with GenAI startup
following a successful pilot program in 2024.
The strategic partnership will see Cleary roll out Legora’s suite of AI-driven services, including new product features, across the firm.

kp.k: AI targets document review, extraction and Word mark-up
kp.d: The article describes Legora as enabling lawyers to complete end-to-end tasks more quickly and accurately. Reported capabilities include reviewing tens of thousands of documents, supporting mark-up in Word, and using Tabular Review for bulk document questions or extractions across up to 100,000 documents in parallel. These are product capability and efficiency claims, not reported findings from a comparative study.
qs: Legora allows lawyers to complete end-to-end tasks more quickly and accurately, enhancing the efficiency of workflows.
Legora helps professionals review tens of thousands of documents and supports mark-up in Word.
Its Tabular Review tool enables the bulk upload of documents to answer specific questions or extractions and can analyse up to 100,000 documents in parallel.

kp.k: Leadership frames AI as efficiency and competitive differentiation
kp.d: Managing partner Michael Gerstenzang presents the partnership as a way to embed AI strategically into workflows, unlock firmwide efficiencies and deliver differentiated, high-quality client work. These are leadership claims about the partnership’s value rather than measured client outcomes.
qs: “Cleary is committed to embedding AI into our workflows in strategic and competitive ways,”
“Partnering with Legora allows us to unlock efficiencies across the firm and deliver differentiated, high-quality work for our clients.”

kp.k: Firm combines external platform adoption with custom AI development
kp.d: The article positions Legora as one component of Cleary’s broader AI integration strategy. Cleary’s acquisition of generative AI product development company Springbok is intended to accelerate innovation and develop custom AI builds for clients and practice groups. The strategy also encompasses ClearyX’s emerging-technology transactional solutions and Practice Innovation’s work to embed AI across legal service delivery.
qs: Legora’s collaborative AI platform is one part of Cleary’s multi-faceted approach to driving AI integration across the firm.
a generative AI product development company, to accelerate innovation at the firm and develop custom AI builds for clients and practice groups.

ClearyX, which focuses on emerging technologies to create efficient, cost-effective transactional solutions for clients; and Practice Innovation is driving towards building AI technology into and across the firm’s delivery of legal services.

kp.k: Deployment prioritises identified, high-value use cases
kp.d: Director of Practice Innovation Ilona Logvinova distinguishes thoughtful integration from simply distributing AI firmwide. She says deployment should engage identified, high-value use cases that enhance client service across practices, teams and regions; the article does not specify those use cases or their selection criteria.
qs: “Our firm is committed to embedding AI in a way that is both strategic and thoughtful,”
“This is not about simply rolling out AI across the firm, but about engaging with identified, high-value use cases that enhance our ability to serve clients across practices, teams, and regions.”

kp.k: Legora expands amid successive law-firm partnership announcements
kp.d: As of publication, the article reports Legora’s use in over 20 countries by over 250 clients, a United States launch in March, and recent partnerships with Mishcon de Reya, Addleshaw Goddard, Harbottle & Lewis and Goodwin. It also reports over $35m in funding. CEO Max Junestrand describes the United States as the most important innovative legal technology market and predicts that firms such as Cleary will lead client-service innovation; that competitive forecast is his view.
qs: Legora officially launched in the United States in March.
It is currently utilized in over 20 countries by over 250 clients.
Harbottle & Lewis and Goodwin all having very recently announced their partnerships with the Stockholm-founded startup.

“Legora is excited to expand our footprint in North America and partner with the pioneering lawyers at Cleary. In this fast-moving market, it will be firms like Cleary who lead the way and innovate in their ability to deliver exceptional client service.”

cl.s: Concrete claim or prediction about how AI changes legal services, the legal profession, or legal markets (or, for a cross-domain source, its own domain)

pts.k: The article reports a firm-wide Legora rollout and claims faster, more accurate legal workflows; Cleary's leaders anticipate efficiency gains and improved client service through targeted AI integration.
pts.d: Legal IT Insider reports that Cleary will roll out Legora's services across the firm. The article describes Legora as enabling faster and more accurate end-to-end tasks, large-scale document review, question answering and extraction, and Word mark-up. Managing partner Michael Gerstenzang says the partnership will unlock efficiencies and differentiated, high-quality client work. Director of Practice Innovation Ilona Logvinova frames integration as targeting identified, high-value use cases rather than merely distributing software. The article also reports that Cleary acquired Springbok to accelerate innovation and develop custom AI for clients and practice groups. Legora CEO Max Junestrand predicts that firms such as Cleary will lead innovation in client service and characterizes the United States as the most important market for innovative legal technology.

cl.s: Evidence basis offered for the claim (data, benchmarks, cases, experience, authority, or none)

pts.k: The source offers a reported successful pilot, product-capability figures, adoption figures and leadership statements, rather than quantified results of improvements to legal work.
pts.d: The article describes Cleary's 2024 pilot as successful but provides no pilot methods, task results or measured savings. It reports a capacity of up to 100,000 documents analysed in parallel and adoption by over 250 clients in over 20 countries. These are capability and adoption claims, not comparative measurements of speed, accuracy or client outcomes. The article also names recent partnerships with Mishcon de Reya, Addleshaw Goddard, Harbottle & Lewis and Goodwin as examples of market uptake. Statements from Cleary's managing partner and innovation director and Legora's CEO supply the authority and strategic rationale for anticipated benefits. No benchmark or independent evaluation of those benefits is presented.

cl.s: Stated or implied timeframe, conditions or qualifications under which the claim holds

pts.k: The May 1, 2025 announcement follows a 2024 pilot; rollout and strategic benefits are prospective, with no completion date specified.
pts.d: The source reports the partnership on May 1, 2025, following a successful pilot in 2024 and Legora's US launch in March 2025. Product capabilities and adoption figures are described as current at publication. Firm-wide deployment and the leadership claims about improved service are forward-looking, without a specified implementation deadline or timetable for benefits. Logvinova qualifies the integration strategy as thoughtful and focused on identified, high-value use cases across practices, teams and regions.

cl.s: Who is affected and how (market segment, role, firm type, clients, or the public)

pts.k: The claimed effects concern Cleary's lawyers and practice groups, their clients, and Legora's expansion in the law-firm technology market.
pts.d: Lawyers and other professionals are described as gaining faster workflows, document-review capacity and Word mark-up support. Cleary's practices, teams and regions are the scope of the planned integration, with clients expected to receive differentiated, high-quality service and custom AI builds. Legora, a legal-technology vendor, gains a firm-wide partnership as part of its North American expansion. The article makes no concrete prediction about lawyer headcount, staffing structures, billing models or access to justice.
